decks.name: LeetCode #347 - Top K Frequent Elements
decks.description: Find the k most frequent elements in an array

cards.question: Top K Frequent Elements: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, return the k most frequent elements. You may return the answer in any order.

solutions.name: Bucket Sort
solutions.explanation: Use bucket sort where each bucket represents a frequency level. Count frequencies, then place numbers into buckets by their frequency. Iterate from highest frequency bucket down to collect k elements. Most efficient solution with linear time.

solutions.timeDescription: Linear time where n is the length of the array. We iterate through the array once to count, once to fill buckets, and at most once more to collect k elements.
solutions.spaceDescription: Linear space for the count map and freq buckets array, both of which can store up to n elements in the worst case.
solutions.exampleWalkthrough: Given [1,1,1,2,2,3] and k=2: Count frequencies: {1:3, 2:2, 3:1}. Create buckets freq[1]=[3], freq[2]=[2], freq[3]=[1]. Iterate from freq[6] down: freq[3]=[1] add 1 to res, freq[2]=[2] add 2 to res, length is 2 so return [1,2].

solutions.name: Sorting
solutions.explanation: Count frequencies, create array of [count, number] pairs, sort by count descending, and take first k elements. Simple approach but less efficient due to sorting overhead.

Create empty dictionary count to store number frequencies
Loop through each number num in nums
Get num from count defaulting to zero, add one to it, and store back in count at key num

Sort arr in place in descending order by first element of each tuple using reverse equals True
Create list res by taking first k elements from arr and extracting the number which is the second element of each tuple
Return res
codeLines: arr = [(cnt, num) for num, cnt in count.items()]
res = [num for cnt, num in arr[:k]]

solutions.name: Min-Heap
solutions.explanation: Use a min-heap to keep only the k most frequent elements. For each unique number, add it to the heap. If heap size exceeds k, remove the minimum. More space-efficient than sorting when k is much smaller than n.

If greater than k, pop and remove the smallest element from heap using heapq heappop
Create list res by iterating through heap and extracting the number which is the second element of each tuple
Return res
codeLines: res = [num for cnt, num in heap]
